title: Book Store accounts - create a user, get a token, sign in and sign out

sourcesRead.contributes: user story, context, account/test-data rules, password policy, out of scope, AC-1..AC-13 (custom field), PO clarification on AC-6

actors: a reader of the Book Store (story.md#L17)
context: The Book Store web site (/login, /profile) and API under /Account/v1 (Swagger UI at /swagger/) let a client create a user account, request an access token and check whether the account is authorized; the same account signs in on the web site (story.md#L23-L25).

acceptanceCriteria.quote: AC-1 (API) Creating a user with `POST /Account/v1/User` and a JSON body `{ "userName", "password" }` whose password satisfies the policy returns **201 Created**. The body contains the new user's id (`userID`, a UUID), `username` equal to the requested user name, and an empty `books` list.
acceptanceCriteria.text: Creating a user with POST /Account/v1/User and a JSON body { "userName", "password" } whose password satisfies the policy returns 201 Created. The body contains the new user's id (userID, a UUID), username equal to the requested user name, and an empty books list.
outcomes: 201 Created
body contains `userID`, a UUID
body `username` equals the requested user name
body `books` is an empty list

acceptanceCriteria.quote: AC-2 (API) A password that does not satisfy the policy (too short, or missing an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a digit or a special character) is rejected with **400**, error `code` "1300" and the message "Passwords must have at least one non alphanumeric character, one digit ('0'-'9'), one uppercase ('A'-'Z'), one lowercase ('a'-'z'), one special character and Password must be eight characters or longer." No account is created (a token cannot be obtained for it).
acceptanceCriteria.text: A password that does not satisfy the policy (too short, or missing an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a digit or a special character) is rejected with 400, error code "1300" and the message "Passwords must have at least one non alphanumeric character, one digit ('0'-'9'), one uppercase ('A'-'Z'), one lowercase ('a'-'z'), one special character and Password must be eight characters or longer." No account is created (a token cannot be obtained for it).
outcomes: each policy violation (too short; no uppercase letter; no lowercase letter; no digit; no special character) → 400
error `code` "1300"

message "Passwords must have at least one non alphanumeric character, one digit ('0'-'9'), one uppercase ('A'-'Z'), one lowercase ('a'-'z'), one special character and Password must be eight characters or longer."
no account is created: a token cannot be obtained for that user name and password

acceptanceCriteria.quote: AC-3 (API) Creating a user whose user name already exists is rejected with **406**, error `code` "1204" and the message "User exists!".
acceptanceCriteria.text: Creating a user whose user name already exists is rejected with 406, error code "1204" and the message "User exists!".
outcomes: error `code` "1204"
message "User exists!"

acceptanceCriteria.quote: AC-4 (API) Creating a user without a user name or without a password is rejected with **400**, error `code` "1200" and the message "UserName and Password required."
acceptanceCriteria.text: Creating a user without a user name or without a password is rejected with 400, error code "1200" and the message "UserName and Password required."
outcomes: without a user name → 400, error `code` "1200", message "UserName and Password required."
without a password → 400, error `code` "1200", message "UserName and Password required."

acceptanceCriteria.quote: AC-5 (API) `POST /Account/v1/GenerateToken` with the correct user name and password returns **200** with a non-empty `token`, `status` "Success", `result` "User authorized successfully." and an `expires` timestamp 7 days after the moment the token was issued.
acceptanceCriteria.text: POST /Account/v1/GenerateToken with the correct user name and password returns 200 with a non-empty token, status "Success", result "User authorized successfully." and an expires timestamp 7 days after the moment the token was issued.
outcomes: `token` is non-empty
`status` "Success"
`result` "User authorized successfully."
`expires` is a timestamp 7 days after the moment the token was issued

acceptanceCriteria.quote: AC-6 (API) `POST /Account/v1/GenerateToken` with a wrong password issues no token: `token` and `expires` are null, `status` is "Failed" and `result` is "User authorization failed."
acceptanceCriteria.text: POST /Account/v1/GenerateToken with a wrong password issues no token: token and expires are null, status is "Failed" and result is "User authorization failed."
outcomes: 401 Unauthorized (PO clarification, story.md#L75)
`token` is null
`expires` is null
`status` "Failed"
`result` "User authorization failed."

acceptanceCriteria.quote: AC-7 (API, security) The token must not disclose the user's password: decoding the token (a JWT) must not reveal the password in any part of it.
acceptanceCriteria.text: The token must not disclose the user's password: decoding the token (a JWT) must not reveal the password in any part of it.
outcomes: the token decodes as a JWT
no part of the decoded token (header, payload, signature) contains the user's password

acceptanceCriteria.quote: AC-8 (API) `POST /Account/v1/Authorized` with `{ "userName", "password" }` returns `false` for a newly created user who has not been issued a token yet, and `true` once a token has been generated for that user. With a wrong password it never returns `true`; it answers with the message "User not found!".
acceptanceCriteria.text: POST /Account/v1/Authorized with { "userName", "password" } returns false for a newly created user who has not been issued a token yet, and true once a token has been generated for that user. With a wrong password it never returns true; it answers with the message "User not found!".
outcomes: newly created user, no token issued yet → `false`
after a token has been generated for that user → `true`
wrong password → never `true`
wrong password → message "User not found!"

acceptanceCriteria.quote: AC-9 (UI + API) On the login page (`/login`), signing in with an account created through the API opens the profile page (`/profile`), which shows "User Name :" followed by that user's name. After this sign-in, `POST /Account/v1/Authorized` returns `true` for the account.
acceptanceCriteria.text: On the login page (/login), signing in with an account created through the API opens the profile page (/profile), which shows "User Name :" followed by that user's name. After this sign-in, POST /Account/v1/Authorized returns true for the account.
outcomes: after signing in, the profile page `/profile` is open
the profile page shows "User Name :" followed by the user's name
`POST /Account/v1/Authorized` then returns `true` for the account

acceptanceCriteria.quote: AC-10 (UI) Signing in with a wrong password keeps the user on the login page and shows the message "Invalid username or password!" in red below the form.
acceptanceCriteria.text: Signing in with a wrong password keeps the user on the login page and shows the message "Invalid username or password!" in red below the form.
outcomes: the user stays on the login page `/login`
message "Invalid username or password!" is shown below the form
the message is shown in red

acceptanceCriteria.quote: AC-11 (UI) Clicking "Login" with an empty user name and an empty password does not sign in; both fields are highlighted as invalid.
acceptanceCriteria.text: Clicking "Login" with an empty user name and an empty password does not sign in; both fields are highlighted as invalid.
outcomes: clicking "Login" with both fields empty does not sign in (the user stays on the login page)
the user name field is highlighted as invalid
the password field is highlighted as invalid

acceptanceCriteria.quote: AC-12 (UI) Clicking "Logout" on the profile page signs the user out and returns to the login page. Opening `/profile` afterwards no longer shows the user name and shows "Currently you are not logged into the Book Store application, please visit the login page to enter or register page to register yourself."
acceptanceCriteria.text: Clicking "Logout" on the profile page signs the user out and returns to the login page. Opening /profile afterwards no longer shows the user name and shows "Currently you are not logged into the Book Store application, please visit the login page to enter or register page to register yourself."

acceptanceCriteria.quote: AC-13 (API) `DELETE /Account/v1/User/{UUID}`, authorized with the user's token, deletes the account and returns **204 No Content**. Afterwards `POST /Account/v1/GenerateToken` for that user name returns `status` "Failed".
acceptanceCriteria.text: DELETE /Account/v1/User/{UUID}, authorized with the user's token, deletes the account and returns 204 No Content. Afterwards POST /Account/v1/GenerateToken for that user name returns status "Failed".
outcomes: DELETE with the user's token → 204 No Content
afterwards `POST /Account/v1/GenerateToken` for that user name returns `status` "Failed"

endpoints.request: JSON body { "userName", "password" } (story.md#L45); response body has userID, username, books (story.md#L45)
user name and password (story.md#L53); request field names not stated for this endpoint (G6)
{UUID} is the user's id (userID from POST /Account/v1/User, story.md#L45); authorized with the user's token (story.md#L69); header scheme not stated (G9)

auth.mechanism: the user's token from POST /Account/v1/GenerateToken authorizes DELETE /Account/v1/User/{UUID}; how it is sent (header name/scheme) is not stated (G9)
auth.credentials: user name created per run; password from environment variable DQ_USER_PASSWORD (story.md#L33)

rules.text: Password policy: at least 8 characters, with at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one digit and one special (non-alphanumeric) character; enforced when an account is created.

Accounts are created through the API (POST /Account/v1/User) with a unique user name per run (for example qa-<timestamp>) and removed afterwards with DELETE /Account/v1/User/{UUID}. Accounts for sign-in are always created through the API.
The password for these accounts is taken from the environment variable DQ_USER_PASSWORD (it satisfies the password policy). Never hard-code a password.

errorModel.body: code "1300", message "Passwords must have at least one non alphanumeric character, one digit ('0'-'9'), one uppercase ('A'-'Z'), one lowercase ('a'-'z'), one special character and Password must be eight characters or longer."

errorModel.case: creating a user whose user name already exists
creating a user without a user name or without a password
GenerateToken with a wrong password or an unknown user name
errorModel.body: token null, expires null, status "Failed", result "User authorization failed."

errorModel.case: UI sign-in with a wrong password
errorModel.body: "Invalid username or password!" in red below the form

testData.strategy: tests create their own accounts through POST /Account/v1/User with a unique user name per run (for example qa-<timestamp>); the password comes from the environment variable DQ_USER_PASSWORD
constraints: accounts for sign-in are always created through the API, not the registration form
testData.cleanup: remove each created account with DELETE /Account/v1/User/{UUID}

outOfScope: The "New User" registration form on the web site (story.md#L40, #L79)

gaps.value: 401 Unauthorized for GenerateToken with a wrong password or an unknown user name; body as in AC-6. AC-8 (Authorized) is unchanged. AC-13's outcome stays as written (status "Failed"); the 401 from L75 also applies to that request since the deleted user name is unknown

gaps.element: how "7 days after the moment the token was issued" is compared: the issue moment is not observable from the client, and the timestamp format/time zone and an acceptable tolerance are not stated

gaps.value: the issue moment is taken as the time the GenerateToken request was sent/answered; `expires` (parsed as an ISO-8601 timestamp, UTC if no offset is given) must be 7 days after that moment, allowing only for clock difference between test client and server (a tolerance of a few minutes, not hours)
